card.name: "in" or "when" after a patient count
card.fires_on: The small word "in" (sometimes "when") right after a noun for a group of subjects or an event, such as "28 women in" or "reported in". It introduces which group, study arm or circumstance applies.

modes.label: Count then group
modes.description: "in" after a number of patients, women or animals, leading into a treatment group.
modes.example: After an average follow-up of 5.2 years, 28 women<< in>> the estrogen-alone group and 19

modes.label: Circumstance link
modes.description: "in" or "when" after a verb or "or", leading into a circumstance such as association with a change or use in a risk group.
modes.example: Monitor patients closely, especially within the first 24-72 hours of initiating therapy or<< when>> used in patients at higher risk.

card.writes: It pushes down words like "repeated", "brief" and "administration", so the next word is less likely to be one of these.
card.plain: It marks the little word "in" that links a count of patients to the study group they were in.
